Author: Paul Spooren <mail@aparcar.org>
Date:   Tue Jun 9 16:53:14 2020 -0400

    LRANK: Add command (the command will be renamed LPOS).
    
    The `LRANK` command returns the index (position) of a given element
    within a list. Using the `direction` argument it is possible to specify
    going from head to tail (acending, 1) or from tail to head (decending,
    -1). Only the first found index is returend. The complexity is O(N).
    
    When using lists as a queue it can be of interest at what position a
    given element is, for instance to monitor a job processing through a
    work queue. This came up within the Python `rq` project which is based
    on Redis[0].
    
    [0]: https://github.com/rq/rq/issues/1197
    
    Signed-off-by: Paul Spooren <mail@aparcar.org>

part.text:
## Answer

**Yes, the option was renamed — it was originally called `FIRST` and was renamed to `RANK`.**

The supporting commit in this repository's history is:

**`a5a3a7bbc61203398ecc1d5b52c76214f5672776`** — *"LPOS: option FIRST renamed RANK."* (antirez, Wed Jun 24 09:07:17 2020 +0200)

The commit message itself states the answer verbatim:

> ```
> LPOS: option FIRST renamed RANK.
> ```

And the diff confirms the mechanical rename, e.g. in `src/t_list.c`:

> ```diff
> -/* LPOS key element [FIRST rank] [COUNT num-matches] [MAXLEN len]
> +/* LPOS key element [RANK rank] [COUNT num-matches] [MAXLEN len]
>  ...
> -        if (!strcasecmp(opt,"FIRST") && moreargs) {
> +        if (!strcasecmp(opt,"RANK") && moreargs) {
>  ...
> -                addReplyError(c,"FIRST can't be zero: use 1 to start from "
> +                addReplyError(c,"RANK can't be zero: use 1 to start from "
> ```

### Supporting history (the full arc)

1. `a7936ef96` "LRANK: Add command (the command will be renamed LPOS)" — command introduced (June 9, 2020).
2. `e63a5ba12` "LPOS: implement the final design." — the option appears as `FIRST` in early examples (June 10, 2020).
3. `89ca2afd6` "LPOS: update to latest proposal." and `0091125ca` "LPOS: tests + crash fix." — still use `FIRST` (e.g. `r LPOS mylist c FIRST 1`).
4. **`a5a3a7bbc` "LPOS: option FIRST renamed RANK."** — the rename (June 24, 2020).
5. Later commits (e.g. `9204a9b2c`, `135998ed8`, `11cf5cbdc`) and the current checkout all use `RANK`.

In the current pinned checkout (`e64d91c37`), the rename is fully settled: `src/t_list.c` parses `opt,"RANK"`, and `src/commands/lpos.json` documents the subcommand argument as `"name": "rank"`.

So your memory is correct: the option was called `FIRST` in the early LPOS examples from June 2020, and it was renamed to `RANK` less than two weeks later.
